item.title: Japan to sidestep 3.5% defence spending target despite US pressure, Asahi reports
item.description: Japan is set to stop short of explicitly adopting a defence spending target of 3.5% of GDP in a planned revision of its national security strategy later this year, despite repeated US calls on ...
item.content:encoded:
Japan to sidestep 3.5% defence spending target despite US pressure, Asahi reports Reuters | Updated: 16-10-2026 05:07 IST | Created: 16-10-2026 05:07 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Japan is set to stop short of explicitly adopting a defence spending target of 3.5% of GDP in a planned revision of its national security strategy later this year, despite repeated US calls on allies to meet that benchmark, the Asahi newspaper reported on Friday. The government is instead leaning toward significantly increasing defence-related spending over the next five years, including broader security expenditures, the report said, citing multiple government sources. Tokyo hopes that a demonstrated commitment to strengthening military capabilities will appease Washington, the report added. The defence ministry did not immediately respond to an emailed request for comment on the report. According to Asahi, US President Donald Trump's administration has repeatedly urged Japan behind closed doors to raise defence spending to 3.5% of GDP, describing the level as a global standard for allies. But formally committing to such a target would pose a major fiscal challenge for Tokyo. Defence spending at 3.5% of GDP would exceed 20 trillion yen ($126.52 billion) annually, requiring substantial new funding sources and likely forcing politically sensitive tax increases, Asahi said. ($1 = 158.0800 yen)

item.title: Nvidia, Apple each gave $25 million for Trump's ballroom, Washington Post reports
item.description: Nvidia and Apple each committed $25 million for US President Donald Trump's planned White House ballroom, according to a Washington Post report on Thursday that showed $333 million in private ...
item.content:encoded:
Nvidia, Apple each gave $25 million for Trump's ballroom, Washington Post reports Nvidia and Apple each committed $25 million for US President Donald Trump's planned White House ballroom, according to a Washington Post report on Thursday that showed $333 million in private donations for the project. Reuters | Updated: 16-10-2026 01:57 IST | Created: 16-10-2026 01:57 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Nvidia and Apple each committed $25 million for US President Donald Trump's planned White House ballroom, according to a Washington Post report on Thursday that showed $333 million in private donations for the project. The Adelson family, longtime financial supporters of Trump and his Republican Party, committed $25 million as well, as did billionaire Charles Ergen, co-founder and chairman of telecommunications company Dish Network, the report added. The president himself is not on the list, according to the Post. Reuters has not verified the report. The White House said it would not release information about the donors, who spokesman Davis Ingle said "represent a wide array of great American companies." "The same critics who are alleging fake conflicts of interests would also complain if American taxpayers were footing the bill for these long-overdue renovations," Ingle told Reuters. Nvidia said it was proud to make a donation to a nonpartisan trust that serves Americans. "As an American company, our support for the United States is paramount, and independent of any business interests," a spokesperson said. Apple declined to comment. The scale of the ballroom project and the administration’s handling of fundraising and disclosures have drawn criticism from watchdog groups and legal experts, who say they raise questions about transparency, donor influence and adherence to longstanding ethics and oversight norms. "The secrecy is a huge problem," said Eric Petry of the Brennan Center for Justice. "When people with business before the government can give millions to the president's pet project, and the public can't see who or how much, there's no way to tell whether they're buying access or favors." Federal contractors including Lockheed Martin Corp, Microsoft Corp and Palantir Technologies Inc all gave $10 million, the Post reported. The companies did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Trump initially said he and wealthy donors would pay for the estimated $400 million project, but he later unsuccessfully sought $1 billion from Congress for an underground bunker and security features to harden the facility. The Post reported that the "vast majority of the funds raised came from companies and wealthy individuals with interests before the federal government" and that half the total came from companies or executives of firms that have had federal government contracts in Trump's second White House term. The planned ballroom is among several projects Trump is pursuing in his efforts to remake Washington with sweeping, unilateral changes that his opponents have challenged in court and called a power grab. The US Supreme Court, in a 5-4 ruling in August, allowed Trump to continue construction of the ballroom while he challenges a judicial order that would halt much of the development. In a dissent, Chief Justice John Roberts said the project was "likely unlawful." The ballroom, which Trump has said will seat 1,000 guests, has faced public backlash. Preservationists and opponents say Trump exceeded his authority by demolishing the historic East Wing, which housed the first lady's offices and the White House movie theater, to make room for the structure. Trump says a planned 90,000-square-foot (8,360-square-meter) White House ballroom will include bomb shelters, medical facilities, defenses against drones and missiles and other security features. Confronted with criticism of the project, his administration now says the facility is needed for national security, an argument the president has also made about a proposed triumphal arch.

item.title: Trump says government won’t livestream execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan
item.description: US President Donald Trump announced that the government will not livestream the firing-squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan, reversing a previous plan by Secretary of War Pete Hegseth ...
item.content:encoded:
Trump says government won’t livestream execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan US President Donald Trump announced that the government will not livestream the firing-squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan, reversing a previous plan by Secretary of War Pete Hegseth following widespread pushback. ANI | Updated: 15-10-2026 21:08 IST | Created: 15-10-2026 21:08 IST

Handout photo of Nidal Hasan, who was convicted in connection with the 2009 Fort Hood shooting. (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US President Donald Trump announced on Thursday that the administration would not broadcast the firing-squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan, withdrawing a proposal initially outlined by Secretary of War Pete Hegseth. While publicly streaming Hasan’s execution “might have been a strong deterrent for the World to witness how America deals with Terrorists and SCUM like Hasan,” Trump stated in a Truth Social post that “many very good and well-meaning people would rather not watch him die, through streaming, or through any other visual device.” “He will die, as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event will not be streamed,” the President stated, noting further that relatives of Hasan’s victims would be permitted to witness the capital punishment in person on December 3. The Army sentenced Hasan, a former major, to death in 2013 following his conviction for killing 13 people and injuring 32 others at the Fort Hood military base in Texas in 2009. Trump's reversal followed substantial criticism from both Republican and Democratic lawmakers after Hegseth stated that Hasan was “going to get a firing squad of soldiers, and we’ll make sure that people are able to watch it.” Following the announcement by the Secretary of War, Vice President JD Vance remarked on the proposed broadcast, “I don’t know that’s going to happen.” Addressing reporters at the White House over the weekend, Trump indicated that he would determine the final outcome. “There are two thoughts: don’t show it and show it. ’Cause you know, by showing it, maybe other people won’t be doing what he did. So I’ll make a decision ultimately. I know what the military would like to do, but I’ll make a decision,” the President stated. During an interview with CBS News earlier this week, House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., expressed apprehension that footage of the execution could serve as propaganda for future extremists. “We’ve got to think through the policy implications of all that,” he stated, adding, “I wouldn’t be watching it if it was aired.” Additionally, the Speaker noted the need to convey the concerns of his Republican congressional colleagues to the White House, observing, “Not everybody is in favour of the idea.” The US military last carried out an execution in 1961 by hanging Army Pvt. John Bennett after his conviction for raping and attempting to murder an 11-year-old girl in Austria. The military's last firing-squad execution occurred in 1945, when Pvt. Eddie Slovik was put to death following a court-martial for desertion during the Second World War. (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
US STOCKS-Wall St set for higher open after strong bank earnings, chip stocks rally (For a Reuters live blog on U.S., UK and European stock markets, click or type LIVE/ in a news window.) * Futures up: Dow 0.51%, S&P 500 0.73%, Nasdaq 0.98% * Bank of America raises NII forecast; Q3 profit beats * Morgan Stanley's third-quarter profit jumps * US chipmakers gain after ASML results (Updates before markets open) By Sukriti Gupta and Twesha Dikshit Oct 15 (Reuters) - Wall Street's main indexes were set to open higher on Wednesday after solid results from Bank of America and Morgan Stanley, while chipmakers climbed as ASML reported strong quarterly results. Reuters | Updated: 15-10-2025 18:37 IST | Created: 15-10-2025 18:37 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

(For a Reuters live blog on U.S., UK and European stock markets, click or type LIVE/ in a news window.) * Futures up: Dow 0.51%, S&P 500 0.73%, Nasdaq 0.98% * Bank of America raises NII forecast; Q3 profit beats * Morgan Stanley's third-quarter profit jumps * US chipmakers gain after ASML results (Updates before markets open) By Sukriti Gupta and Twesha Dikshit Oct 15 (Reuters) - Wall Street's main indexes were set to open higher on Wednesday after solid results from Bank of America and Morgan Stanley, while chipmakers climbed as ASML reported strong quarterly results. Bank of America and Morgan Stanley added 3.8% and 4.1%, respectively, premarket after the top lenders beat Wall Street estimates for third-quarter profit on dealmaking strength. Bank of America also raised the low end of its interest income forecast range. "We've seen really good results from the big banks that have reported thus far, some impressive beats there, so I would expect that we'd see positive sentiment and a good market reaction," said Kristina Hooper, chief market strategist at Man Group. Meanwhile, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said at a CNBC event that the wave of investment into the U.S. economy is sustainable and is only getting started. A day earlier, lenders including Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase reported solid performance in investment banking and predicted that the business would continue to boom. Analysts expect third-quarter earnings growth to be 9.2% year-on-year, slightly higher than the previously forecast 8.8%, according to LSEG I/B/E/S data from Tuesday. Shares of U.S. chipmakers rose after ASML reported third-quarter orders and operating income above market expectations. U.S.-listed shares of ASML were up 4.4%. Micron Technology and Advanced Micro Devices gained 2.6% each, while Intel and Nvidia added 1.7% and 2.6% respectively. At 8:43 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis were up 235 points, or 0.51%, S&P 500 E-minis were up 49 points, or 0.73%, and Nasdaq 100 E-minis were up 242 points, or 0.98%. A slate of Fed officials including governors Stephen Miran and Christopher Waller, Atlanta President Raphael Bostic and Kansas City boss Jeffrey Schmid are set to speak later in the day. Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell left the door open to rate cuts on Tuesday by saying the U.S. labor market remained mired in low-hiring, low-firing doldrums. Fed's Beige Book of economic condition, due at 2:00 p.m. ET, is also on radar. Meanwhile, President Donald Trump on Tuesday said Washington was considering cutting some trade ties with China, including in relation to cooking oil. That came after the two countries began imposing tit-for-tat port fees, adding to concerns about the China-U.S. trade war. Among other stocks, Abbott declined 2.9% after its quarterly revenue fell short of analysts' expectations. BlackRock and a group backed by Nvidia will acquire Aligned Data Centers in a deal worth $40 billion, the companies said. Shares of BlackRock were up 1.1%. U.S.-listed shares of gold miners gained as bullion prices surged past $4,200 an ounce for the first time. Newmont rose 1.8%.
